evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Be accountable for uptime & system integrity – catch ingestion and pipeline issues or logic bugs and resolve them within our SLAs.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Rigour: the responsibilities are built around reliability and consistency, with 'accountable for uptime & system integrity' and 'resolve them within our SLAs' and no shipping-speed language anywhere.
evidence.domain_risk: a deep understanding of claims, eligibility, EHR data, and frameworks such as FHIR and HL7
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: High: the role works directly on regulated healthcare data — 'claims, eligibility, EHR data, and frameworks such as FHIR and HL7' — for a company 'accountable for patient outcomes and overall cost of care'.
evidence.collaboration_width: the pop health team; our engineering team; the performance managers; business and clinical managers
evidence.data_team_maturity: We're hiring our first dedicated data person.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: Early: 'We're hiring our first dedicated data person' makes this the founding data hire, even though an engineering partner has already stood up a platform to inherit.
evidence.jd_authorship: Work within Google Cloud to iterate on our business logic and transformation infrastructure
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Hiring manager: bullets name the actual stack and handover model — 'Work within Google Cloud to iterate on our business logic and transformation infrastructure' and 'Take on systems as they move from our engineering partner into steady state'.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: You report to the VP of Growth and Population Health.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: Commercial: the primary audience is business operators and performance managers — 'our operators can monitor performance across all of our levers' — with the role reporting to 'the VP of Growth and Population Health'.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: Strategic: 'As Data and Analytics Engineer, you own four things' and 'Success in this role means end to end ownership' put direction-setting on the role rather than scoped delivery.
evidence.ai_role: Are AI-native: you live in modern AI tools to support your work
evidence.ai_role_explanation: ai_user: the candidate is expected to use AI tools to accelerate their own work — 'you live in modern AI tools to support your work' — with no requirement to build data for AI systems.
evidence.testing_framing: Data Trust: the business trusts the numbers, and you are ahead of issues rather than behind them
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Responsibility: quality is an owned outcome, not a listed tool — 'Develop monitoring and uptime reporting' and 'Data Trust: the business trusts the numbers' are stated as what the role is measured on.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Data Trust: the business trusts the numbers, and you are ahead of issues rather than behind them
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: High: trustworthiness is the first success measure listed, and the fear named is bad numbers reaching a business that is financially accountable for patient cost of care.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: you would rather take something into production, harden it, and keep improving it than move on to the next greenfield build
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: Fix/scale: the JD explicitly contrasts itself with greenfield work — 'build on our existing data platform, harden it' — and the standout trait is preferring hardening over new builds.
evidence.work_arrangement: Location: New York City strongly preferred (Hybrid). Open to exceptional remote candidates.
evidence.loss_aversion: Risk framing centres on trust in the numbers and system uptime: 'Data Trust: the business trusts the numbers, and you are ahead of issues rather than behind them' sits at the top of the success criteria, alongside 'accountability for uptime & system integrity'.
